question: At a time when another tragedy in the Mediterranean claimed the lives of 60 people when a vessel capsized off the coast of Libya, the European Union is facing allegations that once again leave Frontex shrouded in controversy.

This time, information obtained by a group of journalists from a number of international media outlets indicates that Frontex has sent the coordinates of migrant boats in distress to the most violent Libyan militia: Tareq Bin Zeyad. Reports claim that Frontex shared the coordinates of migrant boats with the militia, which took them back to Libya, where they were used as a commodity for slave labour networks.

At least 1 000 migrants have already been taken back to Libya under these circumstances. Not only is the practice of forced pullbacks illegal under international law, they are too immoral to be allowed to continue unabated. It is not the first episode of this nature.
In the light of these allegations, what investigation will be carried out and how does the Commission intend to put an end to this kind of information sharing?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.4.2024) In a communication of 15 January 2024 to the Chair of the European Parliament’s Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs, the Executive Director of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) explicitly confirmed that Frontex has not been in contact with the ‘Tareq Bin Zeyad’ militia at any time.

When Frontex assets, in the context of patrolling activities, spot a vessel that is unseaworthy or where the lives on board face imminent danger, it activates an emergency procedure to ensure rescue is provided as soon as possible. This includes issuing a ‘Mayday Relay’ call over open radio frequencies, which can be received by any vessel in the vicinity.

Therefore, when Frontex sighted such a vessel on 26 July 2023, it issued a ‘Mayday Relay’. Frontex can only confirm that the call was acknowledged by a Libyan vessel, ‘TBZ’, but not whether this vessel responded to the distress call.
